title: Observability API: failure topology map and synthetic trace probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current error dashboards enumerate counts and SLI breaches but lack a unified failure topology view that connects traces, metrics, and model-level rejections. This makes it difficult for oncall and SREs to quickly determine whether an increase in 5xxs is due to downstream overload, request shaping, KV cache pressure, model runtime exceptions, or transport-level timeouts. Goal: Build a failure topology dashboard and supporting telemetry pipeline plus synthetic trace probes that exercise common request paths. The topology should show causal edges (frontend -> router -> model pool -> storage), with failure types annotated: timeouts, overload/queueing, model rejections (invalid input / decoding errors), model runtime panics/OOM, HTTP/gRPC statuses, network/connectivity errors, and downstream dependency failures. Scope: 1) Trace hook enrichments: new span tags and structured attributes to indicate inferred failure category and resource pressure signals (queue_length, inflight_batches, kv_cache_hit=false, gpu_util_pct). 2) Metric/log pipeline: transforms that emit failure-category counters and time-series of top-N causes per route/model variant. 3) Synthetic trace probes: small, scheduled requests that run through routing and model pools to surface regressions (latency, error-type ratios). 4) Topology dashboard: interactive graph view plus panels for trend lines, per-route breakdown, distribution of failure categories, top offending model versions, and example trace links. Out of scope: full automation of corrective actions (autoscale triggers) for this ticket. Rationale: Combining structured spans + metric transforms + probes will reduce mean time to detect root cause for class B incidents and help validate fallback/rollout policies. The probes also provide consistent sampling for non-user traffic for capacity testing.
acceptance_criteria: Trace hook adds standardized attributes to RPC spans: failure_category, queue_length, inflight_batches, model_version, route_id
Metric pipeline produces per-route per-failure-category time series and counters with <1m latency
Dashboard includes an interactive topology graph and panels for top-5 routes by failure-rate and top-3 failure categories
Synthetic probes run every 5m for selected routes and surface probe-trace links in the dashboard
Oncall runbook updated with guidance mapping dashboard nodes to likely remediation steps
proposed_work: Design schema for failure_category taxonomy (timeout, overload_queue, overload_compute, model_rejection, model_runtime, http_4xx, http_5xx, grpc_non_ok, network_error, downstream_dependency)
Add trace hook instrumentation in router and runtime to tag spans with queue and model signals
Create metric-transform jobs in telemetry pipeline to aggregate span attributes into timeseries and histograms
Implement synthetic probe job (Kubernetes cronjob or Cloud Scheduler) with low-cost model variants
Build Grafana dashboard with topology panel (graph visualization) and drilldown links to sample traces and logs
Create rollout plan: feature flag trace enrichment, pipeline job in staging, probe runbook, then enable in prod for one region
telemetry_changes: New span attributes: failure_category (string), inferred_root_service (string), queue_length (int), inflight_batches (int), kv_cache_hit (bool)
Log enrichment: structured log field 'failure_hint' with evidence (eg. 'timeout-after-10s', 'model-decode-exc')
dashboard_panels: Topology graph with node failure heatmap (node color = failure-rate last 1h)
Time series: failure_category counts (stacked) per route over last 24h
Table: top model_versions by failure_rate with sample trace links
Histogram: queue_length distribution at the moment of failures
Probe heartbeat panel showing latest probe latencies and probe-specific failures
queries_examples: ElasticSearch: logs where failure_hint:"model-decode-exc" and route_id:"payments" sorted by @timestamp desc
Trace link pattern: /traces?query=route_id:orders AND failure_category:model_runtime AND model_version:2025-02-15
